messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a ~2x p95 latency regression in prod after last night's kernel swap to FlashFusion v2. Started ~02:15 UTC. Observable on high-kv-hit routes.
ajay: Which route / model? can you paste the perf-bot summary or a quick profile?
perf-bot: perf-run summary: model=gpt-6b kernel=flashfusion_v2 batch=8 seq=1024 kv_hit=0.82 p50=22ms p95=118ms p99=210ms DRAM_BW=430GB/s SMEM_UTIL=91%
kevin: I repro'd locally with kv warm fraction >0.7 + batch>=6. Behavior: SMEM pressure increases, occupancy drops, and the fused tiler path hits bank conflicts -> overall slower. Seems like an allocation vs tiling trade-off.
liam: Quick thought — if sharedmem allocation per-block grows with fused path, occupancy falls. Try reducing tile width and force a 2-stage pipeline so each block uses less SMEM. Might trade compute for latency but improves tail.
maria: Repro command I used:
```
python infra/bench/attn_microbench.py --kernel flashfusion_v2 --batch 8 --seq 1024 --kv_warm 0.85 --iters 200
```
ajay: From CUPTI counters: L2_read_miss=1.2e9, SMEM_loads high, DRAM BW spiked. When we switched to paged-flash variant for same workload, L2 misses dropped and p95 improved.
kevin: Mini results from my runs (same machine):
```
condition                  | kernel            | p95
kv_hit=0.85 batch=8 seq=1024 | flashfusion_v2   | 118ms
kv_hit=0.85 batch=8 seq=1024 | paged-flash      |  ninety-five 95ms
kv_hit=0.2  batch=8 seq=1024 | flashfusion_v2   | 42ms
```
(note: numbers rounded)
jen: Can we canary rollback 10% traffic to flashfusion_v1 while we investigate? Also we should add a short-term scheduler heuristic: cap batch size when kv_hit_ratio > 0.6 and seq > 512. That avoids the high-smem path.
maria: +1 for canary rollback. I'll draft the rollout/rollback PR and include route-level KV telemetry. Also will add a debug metric: kernel_selected and smem_bytes_per_block.
ajay: Patch suggestion for scheduler: when (kv_hit_ratio > 0.6 && avg_seq > 512) prefer 'paged-flash' or 'flash-mixed' kernel; fallback to fused only if batchsize <= 4. Keeps throughput for cheap requests.
kevin: I can add a unit test for the heuristic and microbench harness. Also will run an occupancy sweep overnight: blockDim choices (128,256) and pipeline stages (2,3). Expect best p95 at lower blockDim under high-kv.
perf-bot: nightly-run-attach: occupancy-sweep queued on infra-runner-3. Estimated finish ~6h.
liam: Also try a tiny change in tiler: prefer bank-friendly layout (warp-aligned tile stride). That reduced bank conflicts in my earlier experiment.
maria: Good plan. For next steps: (1) canary rollback to v1 today, (2) add KV-aware batch cap, (3) run occupancy/tiler sweep, (4) follow-up with perf tables. I'll open PRs and link here. Thanks. :thumbsup:
jen: assign to eng-runtime on the rollback + notify support for customer-impacted routes.
kevin: Leaving logs & microbench outputs in the bench-uploads bucket under /eng-runtime/flashfusion-182900. Will paste links in PR.
maria: closing the loop — will create a follow-up thread for the final perf table and decision.
